The actual geometric and analytic transfer values agree in P2, and no counterexample to the final arithmetic transfer conjecture is claimed. Both unresolved interfaces remain Needs Evidence.

problem_checks.source: PDF pp43?46 Theorem6.15 and unit-denominator Lemma6.10; p56 Proposition9.2
problem_checks.independent_reasoning: Over Q3(i)/Q3, choose r^2=-2, a=r+i so a*bar(a)=-1, J=diag(3,1) and G=[[-2,a],[-3*bar(a),-2]]. Exact algebra gives G*JG=J, detG=1, cyclic e0 and distinct characteristic roots. The untwisted Cayley pair is (-1,af/3) of norm -1/3, whose divisor is empty. Central -1 acts trivially on the Rapoport?Zink moduli, but the unit-denominator pair for -G is (-1,af), of norm -3. Lemma6.10, the actual rank-one special pair and Proposition9.2 give length one. The regular Cartier intersection has a nonzerodivisor 3 and no higher Tor cancellation. Thus the claimed untwisted identity is 1=0.
problem_checks.counterevidence_and_repair: The correct restricted lemma survives. Impose a unit denominator or explicitly twist and recompute the pair. The full repaired general reduction, Theorem6.15(3) and final ATC are not refuted or certified by this example.

problem_checks.independent_reasoning: For n=2,t=0, nearby space <1,3>, g=diag(1,-1), u=(3,1), the eigenvalue difference is a unit, so O_F[g]=O_F x O_F is maximal, and det[u,gu]=-6!=0. Type zero allows only the nonsplit active factor i0=2. The inactive component is integral, the actual fixed component is one formal DVR and its active divisor has length one. The printed all-factor sum is (2+0)/2+(1+1)/2=2. The six supported analytic lattice cosets give (x^2-x+1)(1-x), x=3^s, with derivative -log3, agreeing with the actual geometric length one.
problem_checks.counterevidence_and_repair: Admissibility is already retained by Theorem9.6 and Corollary9.13, so the all-factor formula is genuinely inconsistent with its inputs. Theorem9.14 explicitly uses it. A general corrected sum needs active-type and inactive-integrality conditions; that full formula is not certified. This example confirms the desired transfer identity, not its failure.

problem_checks.source: PDF p54 equation8.11; p86 equation13.5; p89 Proposition13.7 and Theorem13.9
problem_checks.independent_reasoning: On the very-special type-zero P1 component at n=2,t=1, local intersection functions extend to zero with Z value 1 and Y value -q. The two global test functions equal 1 at zero and receive the same prescribed arithmetic Hodge constant. Their theta constants therefore cannot both agree with that same nonzero arithmetic value; the tautological degree -1 locates the Y discrepancy. For the common degree factor kappa, FY+qFZ=(q+1)kappa is a nonzero constant, incompatible with simultaneous exact positive-weight modularity. The explicit Q(sqrt5,i) instance, signatures (1,1)/(2,0), type-one places over 11 and excluded primes2,5 satisfies the stated global hypotheses; log11 is not in the Q-span of log2 and log5.
problem_checks.counterevidence_and_repair: This concerns the exact basic-locus theta/modularity identity. Modularity up to a constant, the separate vertical-annihilator argument and the nonzero theta coefficients survive. Type-two limits also rule out a uniform scalar cure. A complete Y-series vertical/zero-term repair is not established, and the final ATC is not thereby disproved.

problem_checks.source: PDF p18 Proposition3.2/Corollary3.4; p25 reverse implication of Theorem3.26
problem_checks.independent_reasoning: Unitarity imposes norm(u)=h(1-d*bar(d)). Fixed d=0,h=1 and target rank-one regular pair (g,u1)=(1,2) would require a last column (2,0) of norm4 to have norm1. Passing to orbits preserves the obstruction. With z=(1-d)^-1 and alpha=norm(u1)/h, the correct image condition is Tr(z)=1+alpha.
problem_checks.counterevidence_and_repair: For the supported integral alpha case, a nonzero residue-trace solution exists even at q=2 and lifts to a unit z. Variable d then gives the compatible inverse; the nonintegral case is outside lattice support. The intended transfer application has a repair, and no central conclusion is refuted.

problem_checks.independent_reasoning: H=[[5/3,4/3],[4/3,5/3]] is regular unitary for diag(1,-1) with determinant1. Its d=5/3 has valuation -1; every norm-one scalar xi is a unit, so v(1-xi*d)=-1, never zero. An arbitrary Schwartz function is also not invariant under scalar twist: the invariant d separates the two relative orbits, and a compact nonnegative bump supplies a positive/zero orbital-integral distinction for compact U(1) conjugation.
problem_checks.counterevidence_and_repair: The actual lattice characteristic functions are scalar-unit invariant and vanish on the negative-valuation branch. Those restrictions and recomputation of the twisted pair restore the intended use. The unrestricted normalization statement remains false.

problem_checks.independent_reasoning: For X=A_k^3, Cartier center Z=V(z), and reduced Y=V(z) union V(x,y), ideal(xz,yz), the ambient blowup is the identity. The strict transform is the surviving z-axis, with local dimension1 at the origin, whereas dim_0 Y=2. These closed schemes also provide admissible formal special-fiber examples.
problem_checks.counterevidence_and_repair: A surviving-pure-component restriction is needed; nonempty alone is insufficient. The actual regular graph applications use Cartier pullback in Proposition5.17, so their construction is not refuted.

problem_checks.source: PDF p66 proof of Theorem10.8; earlier two-map model in Proposition5.9
problem_checks.independent_reasoning: The displayed scalar field W(k)[1/p] is incompatible with p-nilpotent test rings. Even replacing it by the integral lattice, the single incidence (ell,H)=0 for reduction of diag(p,p,1), n=3,t=2, contains P(radical) x (P2)^dual=P1 x P2 of dimension3, including at the stated linking point, instead of the claimed relative dimension2.
problem_checks.counterevidence_and_repair: The actual polarized local model retains both linked lattice maps with composite p, and a separate semistability interface is cited. Correcting only the scalar ring is insufficient; a correct linked deformation/flat model is required. The actual semistability conclusion is not disproved.
